title: Rational exponents near 3/2
summary: Given a graph $H$, the extremal number $ex(n,H)$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph not containing $H$ as a subgraph. The well-known rational exponents conjecture of Erdős and Simonovits states that for any rational $γ\in (1,2)$ there exists a single bipartite graph $H$ satisfying $ex(n,H)=Θ(n^γ)$. Among other results, the conjecture has been verified for all $γ=1+a/b$, where $b>a^2$, by Jiang and Qiu and for all $γ=2-a/b$, where $b>\max\{a, (a-1)^2\}$, by Conlon and Janzer.
